scenario_title: Agent-Mediated Cross-Department Delegation and Information Aggregation

who.role: authorized employee coordinating with department Agents and cooperating insiders
who.origin: internal human principal with trusted enterprise workflow participants
who.privilege_level: valid source-department access plus purpose-limited temporary or delegated access
who.authorized_principal: the employee role, reporting path, project membership, and approval chain
who.execution_principal: the employee and one or more enterprise Agents performing handoff, retrieval, aggregation, or routing

what: use legitimate project handoffs, temporary delegation, approval relationships, and cooperating Agents to aggregate information across departments beyond the original business purpose

why.details: Each request is framed as a plausible project, handoff, or temporary support activity. The security signal appears only when the organization-wide information flow is reconstructed.

threat_model.attacker_capability: The employee can perform normal work, request collaboration, join a project, receive time-limited permissions, and ask Agents to coordinate or summarize approved workflow steps.
threat_model.security_boundary: A legitimate role, department relationship, approval, or temporary delegation must not be composable into an information path that exceeds the task purpose, dependency graph, or expiry window.
threat_model.excluded_capabilities: The scenario does not require password theft, malware, or a direct exploit of access control.
threat_model.authorized_principal: Each local request may be authorized for a human or Agent principal, while the composed cross-department information flow can still be unauthorized.
threat_model.agent_executor: A coordination or tool Agent may collect, summarize, forward, or stage information under a delegated scope that must be checked at every handoff.
threat_model.organization_dependency: The threat is defined by department ownership, reporting and dependency paths, project purpose, approval chain, and temporary delegation expiry.

how.description: Entered a legitimate cross-department project, handoff, or temporary coverage activity.
how.procedure: The employee receives a role assignment, project membership, approval, or time-limited delegation that makes a limited set of cross-department actions legitimate. The dependency path and expiry must be explicit.
observable_evidence: Approval and delegation scope with expiry
how.impact: The employee gains a plausible organizational path to information owned by another department.

how.description: Requested small pieces of information from several departments through normal communication, approval, and Agent-assisted handoff channels.
how.procedure: The employee and cooperating Agents use project language and trusted relationships to obtain separate documents, records, or summaries. Each request is checked against its local permission, while the global purpose and combined information flow remain unverified.
observable_evidence: Individually valid approvals with a shared target entity or topic
Information requests that depart from the original dependency path
how.impact: Information is distributed across departments before any single event appears clearly malicious.

how.description: Used a coordination Agent to aggregate, summarize, or stage the collected fragments across department scopes.
how.procedure: The coordination Agent combines data from multiple department workflows. The generated trajectory must preserve source department, purpose, approval chain, Agent identity, tool calls, and artifact lineage for every fragment.
observable_evidence: Creation of a combined artifact from unrelated departmental sources
Change in user-resource and workflow centrality
how.impact: The composed artifact has a broader sensitivity and purpose than any local request makes visible.

how.description: Routed the combined artifact to a recipient, repository, or downstream task outside the original dependency path and business purpose.
how.procedure: The employee or Agent forwards, stores, or reuses the aggregate in a context whose role, department, approval, or purpose does not authorize the complete information set.
observable_evidence: Final recipient or repository is outside the project dependency path
Combined artifact lineage and recipient mismatch
Delegation or approval has expired or is too narrow
Single-account logs cannot explain the full cross-department path
how.impact: The organization loses control of aggregated information even though the component accesses were authorized locally.

research_questions: Can organization-aware trajectories distinguish normal collaboration from workflow abuse when every individual request is plausible?
Does hierarchical scheduling produce more realistic approval, handoff, and department-dependency constraints than an all-hands planner?
Can detectors identify a distributed threat whose evidence is split across departments, Agents, and workdays?
Does Agent delegation increase the reachable information set beyond the employee purpose even when each local permission check succeeds?
framework_refs: NIST SP 800-162: Attribute Based Access Control
OWASP Agentic Applications Top 10 2026: Identity and Privilege Abuse
OWASP Agentic Applications Top 10 2026: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
MITRE ATT&CK: Valid Accounts, Account Manipulation, and Data from Information Repositories

organization_constraints.purpose: Define whether a locally valid action is valid for this organizational context and whether its composed information flow remains within the authorized business purpose.
fixed_for_matched_pairs: employee roles, reporting paths, and baseline permissions
project goal, task purpose, and schedule context
tool inventory and initial enterprise state
constraints: subject and Agent identity must be linked to role, department, and runtime
resource access must respect department ownership and data classification
delegation and approval must be scoped to purpose and validity window
cross-department handoffs must follow an explicit dependency or approval path
skill and memory reuse must respect origin scope, current scope, tenancy, and expiry

agent_context.human_principal: employee or cooperating insider who initiates, approves, or triggers the task
agent_context.agent_principal: enterprise Agent that plans, retrieves memory, delegates, or calls tools

provenance_requirements: human task intent and task purpose
organization graph path and department ownership
employee role and current permission decision
Agent identity, runtime identity, and session
input/source provenance and memory or skill provenance
plan step, tool call, result, recipient, and resulting state change

counterfactual_design.baseline_pair: Generate benign and threat trajectories from the same organization state and initial schedule.
fixed_variables: model configuration and random seed where supported
counterfactual_design.single_intervention: Change only the department dependency path, approval scope, temporary delegation, or Agent handoff while fixing employee profiles, schedules, source objects, project goal, and initial permissions.
